decision_rows.concept: Does a loss make you keep playing, or stop for the day?
decision_rows.estimand: per-player difference in context-adjusted probability that another match follows inside the session, after a loss versus after a win
decision_rows.expected_publication_reach: roughly a quarter of information-eligible users at the provisional bar; structurally near-universal
decision_rows.inherited_or_novel: inherited (Post-Loss), recast from outcome to behaviour
decision_rows.justification: Calibrated null on both splits, the highest structural reach in the set, real heterogeneity that is not an artefact of shrinkage, chronological stability far above the control band, and per-player estimates that survive every declared probe at rho >= +0.92
decision_rows.main_confounders: time of day, real-life schedule, accumulated session length, right-censoring
decision_rows.narrative_quality: high - immediately recognisable, non-judgemental, no good/bad reading
decision_rows.null_model_viability: STRONG. Within-player circular shift of the arm labels preserves the real serial dependence exactly and measures 0.0508/0.0099 on DISCOVERY and 0.0525/0.0104 on CANDIDATE_TEST against nominal 0.05/0.01
decision_rows.primary_failure_risk: right-censoring at the observation edge and the session-gap convention
decision_rows.report_time_cost: history only; one linear pass per player, milliseconds
decision_rows.unit_of_observation: one in-session match with a known successor state

decision_rows.concept: After a loss, do you change hero or run it back?
decision_rows.distinctiveness: high; no |rho| above 0.30 with any other frozen candidate
decision_rows.estimand: per-player difference in context-adjusted probability the next hero differs, after a loss versus after a win
decision_rows.expected_publication_reach: roughly a fifth of information-eligible users at the provisional bar; structurally near-universal
decision_rows.inherited_or_novel: inherited (Post-Loss), recast from outcome to behaviour
decision_rows.justification: The strongest heterogeneity-to-noise ratio among the calibrated families (tau 0.107, I2 0.845), chronological stability +0.78/+0.74, and the single-draft/random-draft contamination discovery worried about moves the per-player estimate by rho +0.993 - that is, not at all
decision_rows.main_confounders: hero pool size, mode, party role assignment, non-chosen draft modes
decision_rows.narrative_quality: high - a concrete, visible act the player will recognise
decision_rows.null_model_viability: STRONG. Circular-shift null measures 0.0500/0.0091 on DISCOVERY and 0.0480/0.0087 on CANDIDATE_TEST
decision_rows.primary_failure_risk: hero-pool size is a lurking third variable that is not in the projection
decision_rows.report_time_cost: history only; one linear pass per player, milliseconds

decision_rows.concept: When you lose, do you jump straight back in or take a breath?
decision_rows.estimand: per-player difference in context-adjusted log gap to the next match, loss versus win
decision_rows.expected_publication_reach: roughly a fifth of information-eligible users at the provisional bar; structurally near-universal
decision_rows.inherited_or_novel: inherited (Post-Loss), recast from outcome to behaviour
decision_rows.justification: Statistically it is as sound as the two A candidates. It is graded B for two material tradeoffs: it is the most session-gap-sensitive family in the set (rho +0.913 and tau 0.219 -> 0.263 at a 6 h gap) and it overlaps session continuation at rho -0.58, so a portfolio should carry one of the two, or one family with two facets
decision_rows.main_confounders: queue times, party regrouping, time of day, post-game screen length
decision_rows.narrative_quality: high - 'you are a chaser' is a strong, legible line
decision_rows.null_model_viability: STRONG. 0.0488/0.0100 on DISCOVERY and 0.0481/0.0085 on CANDIDATE_TEST
decision_rows.primary_failure_risk: portfolio redundancy with session continuation, plus definitional sensitivity
decision_rows.report_time_cost: history only; one linear pass per player, milliseconds

decision_rows.concept: Do you die more when you step off your comfort heroes?
decision_rows.distinctiveness: good; rho -0.36 with transfer_activity, its own rejected sibling
decision_rows.estimand: per-player difference in context-adjusted deaths per ten minutes, stretch heroes versus comfort-pool heroes
decision_rows.expected_publication_reach: likely low - about 8% of information-eligible users at the provisional bar
decision_rows.inherited_or_novel: inherited (Transfer), recast from outcome to a within-player behavioural contrast
decision_rows.justification: The only Transfer form that survives confirmation: chronological stability +0.467 on DISCOVERY and +0.552 on CANDIDATE_TEST, both clear of the control band. Its tradeoff is real - only 39/495 and 20/257 players clear the provisional bar, and the hero-in-projection question must be settled before the estimand can be called final
decision_rows.main_confounders: hero difficulty, position, pool size; death rate is strongly hero-linked
decision_rows.narrative_quality: high - the idea is vivid and the direction is meaningful
decision_rows.null_model_viability: STRONG but slightly conservative. 0.0488/0.0082 on DISCOVERY, 0.0447/0.0086 on CANDIDATE_TEST
decision_rows.primary_failure_risk: the context projection contains hero, which is close to the treatment itself; removing it raises tau by 55% and chronological stability from +0.47 to +0.61, so the estimand is not yet pinned down
decision_rows.report_time_cost: history only; one linear pass per player, milliseconds
decision_rows.unit_of_observation: one product-context match after a 50-match comfort-pool warm-up

decision_rows.concept: How far into a game are you when your build comes together?
decision_rows.estimand: per-player mean context-adjusted normalised game progress at the eighth item purchase
decision_rows.expected_publication_reach: likely high among parsed-eligible research accounts (44/68 and 27/60 clear the provisional bar) but only 11% of sampled accounts, which is a corpus artefact rather than a candidate property
decision_rows.justification: The strongest heterogeneity in the set (I2 0.969, chronological stability +0.94 and +0.87) and the highest qualified share of any candidate. It is B rather than A because it is a level family whose p-value is not certifiable, because it rests on an unverified item vocabulary, and because parsed dependence caps its research reach
decision_rows.main_confounders: consumables inflate early counts, unverified item vocabulary, position, game length
decision_rows.null_model_viability: WEAK. Calibrated under an i.i.d. null (0.0559/0.0110 and 0.0485/0.0100) but anticonservative once dependence is planted (0.083/0.020 at range 100, 0.199/0.079 at range 200), and its measured dependence ratio is 4.65 at b=100
decision_rows.primary_failure_risk: item semantics are unverified in the capability atlas, so the eighth purchase may be counting consumables; and the level-family standard error cannot be certified at any block length this corpus supports
decision_rows.report_time_cost: parsed detail required; moderate - one sort of the purchase list per match
decision_rows.unit_of_observation: one parsed product-context match with at least eight purchases

decision_rows.concept: How often do you reach for a hero you have not touched in a month?
decision_rows.estimand: per-player mean context-adjusted rate of playing a hero unseen in the previous 30 days
decision_rows.expected_publication_reach: moderate, but on an uncertified p-value
decision_rows.justification: Discovery's own worry is confirmed and is not fixable by the adjustment it proposed: the per-player estimate correlates -0.526 with log match volume, and capping exposure at 500 matches only moves that to -0.349. Its test is not calibrated under any null tested. Interesting, not shippable as it stands
decision_rows.main_confounders: match volume above all; hero pool size; patch-driven pool churn
decision_rows.null_model_viability: BROKEN. Anticonservative under every null tested, including the i.i.d. one (0.0757/0.0194 on DISCOVERY, 0.0655/0.0137 on CANDIDATE_TEST), and it carries the largest measured dependence in the set at 5.25
decision_rows.primary_failure_risk: it is substantially a measure of how much you play
decision_rows.report_time_cost: history only; one linear pass per player
decision_rows.unit_of_observation: one product-context match after a 30-match warm-up

decision_rows.concept: Do your games run long or end early?
decision_rows.estimand: per-player mean context-adjusted log match duration
decision_rows.expected_publication_reach: high on the point estimate, but on an uncertified p-value
decision_rows.justification: Discovery flagged this as its weakest justification and the flag was right. A player's Turbo-only and standard-only estimates agree at only rho +0.495 across 168 players, against a within-mode reliability near +0.99 - so the pooled number is substantially a mode-mix statistic, not one personal tempo. Its test is also the most anticonservative in the set on the confirmation split
decision_rows.main_confounders: game mode (41% of raw variance), lobby type (34%), and nine other players
decision_rows.null_model_viability: BROKEN. Calibrated under an i.i.d. null only; 0.115/0.039 at dependence range 25 on DISCOVERY and 0.171/0.076 on CANDIDATE_TEST, rising to 0.30/0.15 at range 200
decision_rows.primary_failure_risk: it is a ten-player outcome attributed to one player, and half of it is mode mix

decision_rows.concept: Are you a one-position player or a fill player?
decision_rows.estimand: per-player mean context-adjusted probability the position changes between them
decision_rows.expected_publication_reach: likely low: 37 of 116 parsed-eligible DISCOVERY accounts and 32 of 119 on CANDIDATE_TEST reach information eligibility
decision_rows.justification: Statistically healthy where it applies - I2 0.933, chronological stability +0.80 and +0.83 - but honest block geometry leaves it reaching 32% and 27% of parsed-eligible accounts. A good idea that this corpus cannot support
decision_rows.main_confounders: hero is nearly collinear with position; party role assignment; doubled parsed selection
decision_rows.narrative_quality: high - one of the most legible ideas in the set
decision_rows.null_model_viability: MIXED. Calibrated to dependence range 25, anticonservative beyond it
decision_rows.primary_failure_risk: requiring two consecutive parsed matches compounds parsed selection and destroys reach
decision_rows.report_time_cost: parsed detail required for two consecutive matches; trivial compute
decision_rows.unit_of_observation: one pair of consecutive in-session parsed matches

decision_rows.concept: Is your game an early game or a late game?
decision_rows.estimand: per-player mean context-adjusted normalised-progress centroid of own kill and assist times
decision_rows.expected_publication_reach: moderate among parsed-eligible accounts, 11% of sampled
decision_rows.justification: Real and stable, but the per-player spread runs from -0.015 to +0.014 of game progress - about half a minute either side of the population centroid in a 40-minute game. That is too small to narrate honestly, and the null degraded between the two splits
decision_rows.main_confounders: hero, position and role; assist events are timing-only by atlas rule
decision_rows.null_model_viability: WEAK and worse on confirmation: 0.0489/0.0114 at range 25 on DISCOVERY but 0.0946/0.0260 on CANDIDATE_TEST
decision_rows.primary_failure_risk: the effect is tiny in player-facing units
decision_rows.unit_of_observation: one parsed product-context match with at least three own fight events

decision_rows.concept: Do you play more quietly on unfamiliar heroes?
decision_rows.distinctiveness: low: rho -0.36 with transfer_risk, which says the same thing better
decision_rows.estimand: per-player difference in context-adjusted kills-plus-assists per ten minutes, stretch versus comfort
decision_rows.justification: Chronological split-half falls from +0.390 on DISCOVERY to +0.176 on CANDIDATE_TEST, which is inside the planted negative control's own chronological band of -0.073 to +0.218. Only 6-7% of players clear the provisional bar. This is a confirmation failure, and tuning it would be exactly the rescue the phase forbids
decision_rows.null_model_viability: STRONG - the test is fine; the signal is not
decision_rows.primary_failure_risk: chronological stability fails on the confirmation split
decision_rows.unit_of_observation: one product-context match after a 50-match comfort-pool warm-up

decision_rows.concept: When your team is decided ahead or behind at the midpoint, does the game convert?
decision_rows.distinctiveness: low - it correlates diffusely with several unrelated families, a noise signature
decision_rows.estimand: per-player difference in context-adjusted win indicator, decided-ahead versus decided-behind
decision_rows.justification: 5 of 109 and 5 of 112 players clear the provisional bar against a measured Type-I of 1.4% and 1.0% - that is at most a couple of players' worth of signal. Chronological stability +0.366 and +0.305 sits at the control band's edge. It is the outcome form of a family whose outcome form discovery already killed
decision_rows.main_confounders: the arm explains 27.9% of raw variance; four teammates share the trajectory
decision_rows.null_model_viability: ADEQUATE but the observed rejection rate barely exceeds it
decision_rows.primary_failure_risk: the response is a match outcome and the estimand is team-level by construction
decision_rows.unit_of_observation: one parsed match whose midpoint net-worth lead exceeds 5,000 gold

decision_rows.concept: After a lost lane, does your late-game involvement hold up?
decision_rows.distinctiveness: high but irrelevant at this signal level
decision_rows.estimand: per-player difference in context-adjusted own fight events per ten minutes of the second half of game progress, lost lane versus won lane
decision_rows.justification: 4 of 113 on DISCOVERY and 2 of 113 on CANDIDATE_TEST clear the provisional bar against a measured Type-I of exactly 1.0% - the confirmation is indistinguishable from the null. I2 is 0.236 despite a large tau, because the response scale is large, not because players differ. The rejection is now on the record with a proper test, which is what discovery asked for
decision_rows.main_confounders: lane outcome is a team verdict, not a player verdict; hero and position
decision_rows.null_model_viability: STRONG - 0.0507/0.0102 and 0.0498/0.0100; the test is not the problem
decision_rows.primary_failure_risk: there is no between-player signal to find
decision_rows.unit_of_observation: one parsed match with a resolvable own-lane verdict
